name: parameter-object
intent: Bundle a recurring group of parameters that keep travelling together into one cohesive value type, so signatures name a single concept instead of repeating an ordered argument list at every call site.
problem: The same cluster of values - a date range, an address, connection settings, a bunch of flags - is threaded through one method signature after another: every call site must remember the argument order, same-typed values can be swapped silently, and the shared meaning of the cluster stays implicit while the group changes.
context: Local method, constructor and delegating-call structure inside a module or component, where a data clump recurs - usually because the values really are one concept (range, coordinates, credentials) rather than because one method happens to need several values. Applies to object-oriented and functional code alike; the cost differs sharply by language: a record or data class makes the carrier nearly free, while C forces the type, its initialization and its comparison to be written by hand.
benefits: Signatures name the concept: one parameter of a well-named type replaces an ordered list whose meaning otherwise lives only in the reader's head.
Signature stability: adding a member changes the carrier's declaration, not every callee signature, and optional members keep existing construction sites compiling.
Argument-order mistakes disappear, and same-typed values (two strings, three booleans) can no longer be swapped unnoticed.
The group gets one home for defaults, validation and group-level behaviour (contains, overlaps, distance), so those rules are written and tested once.
Tooling works on the group: navigation, rename, refactoring and generated documentation all target one declaration instead of N parameter lists.
Delegation chains stop re-listing the arguments - the carrier is forwarded as one value through every layer.
tradeoffs: A new type must be named and maintained; a vague name or a bundle of only loosely related members hides meaning worse than the parameter list it replaced.
Every call site must construct the object first: extra allocation in garbage-collected languages, copying in languages that pass structs by value, and more setup ceremony for one-off calls.
A shared mutable carrier invites the callee to write into it or the caller to mutate it after the call, so arguments become hidden shared state unless immutability is enforced deliberately.
Coupling is stronger than to loose parameters: members that travel together now evolve together, and users of the type who need only part of the group are dragged along by every addition.
It can mask an over-responsible method: bundling twelve values into one object makes the underlying design problem harder to see.
The refactoring itself churns every call site, and in languages without generated equality or named construction it drags in boilerplate for constructors, accessors and comparison.

participants.responsibility: The cohesive value type that carries the former parameter group; it names the concept, defines which members exist and their order, defaults and optionality, and owns validation and group-level behaviour where the language allows.
The code that constructs the object (positionally, by name or through a factory) and passes it as a single argument; it no longer depends on argument order or on the callee's parameter list.
The method or constructor that declares one parameter of the object's type and reads its named members instead of positional arguments; its signature stays stable as the group's members grow.

use_cases: Data clumps that recur across several signatures: date ranges or periods, coordinates and rectangles, addresses or full names, money plus currency, connection settings.
Groups threaded through a delegation chain, where each layer re-lists the same arguments on the way down and the same values on the way back up.
Public or library APIs that must evolve: a new optional member can be added without breaking existing callers, and named construction documents each value at the call site.
Component configuration where several optional knobs travel together and defaults matter more than the individual values.
Validated value concepts whose invariants (start <= end, non-empty, within range) belong to the group rather than to every operation that consumes it.

AWS SDK for Java 2.x operation requests such as immutable PutItemRequest objects passed to DynamoDbClient.putItem show a library API using one named, evolving carrier instead of repeating operation arguments.
Kubernetes client-go list/watch calls pass a metav1.ListOptions carrier, whose selectors, pagination and watch controls travel together and can be consistently tweaked by informer factories.
Google Cloud Storage's generated Java client exposes GetObjectRequest as a typed protobuf request carrier with a builder, grouping bucket/object and related request data before execution.
avoid_when: The method takes one or two values that do not recur: positional parameters (or a pair/tuple type) stay clearer than a type introduced for a single call site.
The values are only incidentally passed together: a junk-drawer object makes the coupling look intentional, so split them or group only the cohesive subset.
Only argument-order confusion is the problem: named or keyword arguments (Kotlin, Swift, Python, Ruby, C#, Scala) remove it without introducing a type.
A construction has many optional and defaulted settings: builder or functional options express 'optional and defaulted' better than a carrier with a dozen nullable fields.
The group is already a domain concept with rules and a lifecycle: model it as a value object or entity (or a data transfer object at a boundary) rather than as a bare parameter carrier.
anti_patterns: The junk-drawer parameter object: unrelated parameters bundled together just to satisfy a parameter-count limit or a linter.
Passing one 'context' or 'params' object through every layer - it becomes an implicit global, and each callee must guess which of its members it is allowed to touch.
A mutable carrier that the callee writes into to 'return' extra values, instead of returning a result: aliasing and action at a distance.
Extracting a carrier for a single call site, or wrapping a single primitive in a type (the mirror image of Primitive Obsession).
Letting the carrier accumulate behaviour, caches and collaborators until it is a god object rather than a value.
design_principles: Naming as design: values that keep travelling together are a concept, and unnamed concepts are where misunderstandings hide.
Cohesion: members of the carrier must belong to one concept - the grouping is justified by meaning, not by the convenience of one call.
Encapsulation: the carrier is a value, so construct it complete, validate on construction and keep it immutable.
DRY: one declaration of a repeated parameter group, instead of N copies that drift apart as the group changes.
Stable interfaces: the method signature stays closed for modification while the carrier's shape evolves (open for extension).
Separation of concerns: transporting a group of values (the carrier) is distinct from what the operation does with them.
best_practices: Name the type after the concept the values represent (DateRange, Address, ConnectionSettings), never after its role in one method (Params, Args, Data).
Make it immutable (frozen/readonly/val/final/const) and validate invariants in the constructor; a carrier mutated after the call is a bug factory.

Introduce it incrementally: add the object as an extra parameter, construct it from the existing arguments, replace uses one by one, then delete the old parameters (Fowler's mechanics), keeping the suite green at each step.
Move group-level behaviour onto the carrier (contains, overlaps, distanceTo) once it exists, instead of re-deriving the same rules at each call site.
Keep the carrier short-lived and pass it by reference or borrow (value types only for small groups); never park it in long-lived state just because it was convenient.
Split the type when different callers need disjoint subsets, and let each subset keep its own name; a shared carrier that grows for everyone is the junk drawer again.
Use defaults in the carrier or the language's named/optional arguments instead of overload chains, nullable members that mean 'unset', or boolean parameter flags.
sources: Kent Beck, Implementation Patterns (Addison-Wesley, 2007) - Parameter Object, pp. 57-58.
Martin Fowler, Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code, 2nd ed. (2018) - Introduce Parameter Object.
